# OpenCode CLI - Integration Patterns

How cli-opencode positions itself relative to the three sibling cli-* skills, the three documented use cases (per ADR-002), the smart-router decision tree that picks between them, and the self-invocation guard that protects against circular dispatch (per ADR-001).

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).

### When to Use

cli-opencode resolves this by documenting THREE orthogonal use cases. The smart router selects between them based on the calling AI's runtime context.

| Use case | Calling runtime | Target | Self-invocation? |
|----------|-----------------|--------|------------------|
| 1. External runtime to OpenCode | Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell | OpenCode for full plugin / skill / MCP runtime | No |
| 2. In-OpenCode parallel detached session | OpenCode itself (TUI / web / serve / acp) | New OpenCode session via `--port N` (OpenCode 1 only, no OpenCode 2 `run` form, see `./install-and-versions.md`) | No (different session id) |
| 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |

The cycle ADR-001 protects against is the operator inside OpenCode asking cli-opencode to "delegate this exact prompt to OpenCode". That case is REFUSED at the routing layer.

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. USE CASE 1: EXTERNAL RUNTIME TO OPENCODE

### When to use

The calling AI is Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, or a raw shell. The task needs the project's full plugin / skill / MCP runtime, not just a raw model dispatch. Examples:

- Run the ripgrep retrieval recipes from `system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` against the project's spec docs
- Call Code Graph for semantic code search across the repo
- Dispatch a `@deep-research` or `@deep-review` agent loop with externalized state
- Run a sub-agent that needs the continuity ladder (`handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then packet-first spec docs) across iterations

### Smart-router signal

ADR-001's detection signal does NOT trip (no OPENCODE_* env var, no opencode parent process, no live state lock).

What `opencode run` brings that the sibling cli-* dispatches do not. Each capability includes the invocation shape and the use case where it pays off. Each shape is shown for OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), with the OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) form beside it where one exists and a link to `./install-and-versions.md` where one does not.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

The sibling cli-* skills (cli-claude-code, cli-codex) dispatch a raw model or external autonomous CLI behind a thin wrapper. The dispatched tool loads no OpenCode project plugin runtime, no OpenCode skills, and no MCP tools unless the calling AI manually attaches files or pastes context.

`opencode run` is different. It spawns a full OpenCode session. That session loads:

1. Every plugin registered in the project's `opencode.json`
2. Every skill under `.skilled/skills/`
3. Every MCP tool wired through `opencode.json` and `.utcp_config.json`
4. The project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instructions
5. The project's spec folders and their continuity docs

The cli-opencode skill exists because no sibling provides this. It is the bridge between an external AI and the full plugin / skill / MCP runtime this repo defines.

### When to Use

- A dispatch needs the project's plugin, skill or MCP runtime (§2)
- The task needs a parallel detached session (§3)
- The calling AI must parse a structured event stream instead of prose (§4)
- The dispatch must run as a named agent definition (§5)
- The dispatch must target another repository's runtime (§6)

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. FULL PLUGIN, SKILL, AND MCP RUNTIME

### What it does

When `opencode run` starts a session, the runtime loads every plugin, skill, and MCP server the project configures. The dispatched agent has access to:

- All `Skill` invocations the calling AI has access to (system-spec-kit, sk-doc, `sk-code` surface routing, etc.)
- All MCP tools (the Skill Advisor's routing tools, and Code Mode's manuals for ClickUp / Figma / GitHub / Notion / Obsidian and the other external services)
- Every project-local plugin
- The repo's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instruction set as the system prompt

Whether OpenCode 2 loads the same runtime is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.

# OpenCode CLI - Agent Delegation

How cli-opencode routes dispatches to specialized OpenCode agents via the `--agent <slug>` flag. The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes it.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

OpenCode agents are markdown files under `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`. Each file's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, system prompt, and behavioral constraints. When `opencode run --agent <slug>` is invoked, the dispatched session inherits all of that.

The cli-opencode skill exposes the project's full agent roster. The calling AI selects the right slug based on the task type. The agent then shapes the dispatched session: different model, different tool permissions, different system prompt.

### When to Use

- A dispatch needs a role other than the default agent.
- The task type picks the slug: codebase exploration, documentation generation, code review, root-cause debugging, or a command-owned research or review loop (§4 maps each to its invocation shape).

### Discovery commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `opencode agent list` | List all registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
| `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Print resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
| `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Print skill resolution if the agent loads one |

OpenCode loads `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. On OpenCode 1.19.3, user-level agents fall back from `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`), `~/.opencode/` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when the project file is missing. Which of those OpenCode 2.0.32 reads is unverified. The `debug agent` subcommand prints the merged result so the calling AI can confirm which file the dispatch will load.

### Orchestration principle

The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes the task. The calling AI always validates and integrates the output.

This separation of concerns is load-bearing for the cli-opencode skill: the calling AI owns the task graph and the integration step, while the dispatched OpenCode session owns the per-task execution under the agent's tool permissions and system prompt.

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL

### Invocation pattern

On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. # OpenCode CLI - Install and Version Layouts

How to put OpenCode 2.1.4 on a machine, optionally alongside OpenCode 1.19.4 as a fallback, and how to tell which version a name runs.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This reference is the skill's install guidance. OpenCode 2 is the version this repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is a backwards-compatible fallback kept only because not every user has updated yet. A dispatch needs a known binary, and the two supported majors are separate npm packages that both claim the name `opencode`.

### When to Use

- Installing OpenCode 2.1.4, alone or side by side with the `opencode1` launcher for v1
- Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated
- Deciding whether Homebrew, mise or a second npm prefix is the right channel
- Working out why a bare `opencode` runs the version you did not expect

### Claim Labels

Claims in the prose carry one of three labels. The layout table in section 3 summarises the sections below it, whose claims are labelled there.

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `[confirmed]` | Observed on this machine on 2026-10-18 with the command named in the sentence. |
| `[documented]` | Stated by a named source: the official v2 docs at [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/), the launcher comment in `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, the CLI's own `--help` output, or the npm registry. |
| `[unknown]` | Not probed. Treat it as open and do not plan around it. |

### The Fact Behind Every Collision

Both majors ship a binary named `opencode` [confirmed: `npm view opencode-ai bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe' }` and `npm view @opencode/cli bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe', opencode2: 'bin/opencode.exe' }`]. One prefix therefore cannot hold both versions under that name. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the name `opencode`, and v1 is the one that moves: side by side it answers only to the `opencode1` launcher. The second v2 name, `opencode2`, is retired in that layout.

# OpenCode CLI - Integration Patterns

How cli-opencode positions itself relative to the three sibling cli-* skills, the three documented use cases (per ADR-002), the smart-router decision tree that picks between them, and the self-invocation guard that protects against circular dispatch (per ADR-001).

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).

### When to Use

cli-opencode resolves this by documenting THREE orthogonal use cases. The smart router selects between them based on the calling AI's runtime context.

| Use case | Calling runtime | Target | Self-invocation? |
|----------|-----------------|--------|------------------|
| 1. External runtime to OpenCode | Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell | OpenCode for full plugin / skill / MCP runtime | No |
| 2. In-OpenCode parallel detached session | OpenCode itself (TUI / web / serve / acp) | New OpenCode session via `--port N` (OpenCode 1 only, no OpenCode 2 `run` form, see `./install-and-versions.md`) | No (different session id) |
| 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |

The cycle ADR-001 protects against is the operator inside OpenCode asking cli-opencode to "delegate this exact prompt to OpenCode". That case is REFUSED at the routing layer.

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. USE CASE 1: EXTERNAL RUNTIME TO OPENCODE

### When to use

The calling AI is Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, or a raw shell. The task needs the project's full plugin / skill / MCP runtime, not just a raw model dispatch. Examples:

- Run the ripgrep retrieval recipes from `system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` against the project's spec docs
- Call Code Graph for semantic code search across the repo
- Dispatch a `@deep-research` or `@deep-review` agent loop with externalized state
- Run a sub-agent that needs the continuity ladder (`handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then packet-first spec docs) across iterations

# OpenCode CLI - Unique Capabilities

What `opencode run` brings that the sibling cli-* dispatches do not. Each capability includes the invocation shape and the use case where it pays off. Each shape is shown for OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), with the OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) form beside it where one exists and a link to `./install-and-versions.md` where one does not.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

The sibling cli-* skills (cli-claude-code, cli-codex) dispatch a raw model or external autonomous CLI behind a thin wrapper. The dispatched tool loads no OpenCode project plugin runtime, no OpenCode skills, and no MCP tools unless the calling AI manually attaches files or pastes context.

`opencode run` is different. It spawns a full OpenCode session. That session loads:

1. Every plugin registered in the project's `opencode.json`
2. Every skill under `.skilled/skills/`
3. Every MCP tool wired through `opencode.json` and `.utcp_config.json`
4. The project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instructions
5. The project's spec folders and their continuity docs

The cli-opencode skill exists because no sibling provides this. It is the bridge between an external AI and the full plugin / skill / MCP runtime this repo defines.

### When to Use

- A dispatch needs the project's plugin, skill or MCP runtime (§2)
- The task needs a parallel detached session (§3)
- The calling AI must parse a structured event stream instead of prose (§4)
- The dispatch must run as a named agent definition (§5)
- The dispatch must target another repository's runtime (§6)

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. FULL PLUGIN, SKILL, AND MCP RUNTIME

### What it does

When `opencode run` starts a session, the runtime loads every plugin, skill, and MCP server the project configures. The dispatched agent has access to:

- All `Skill` invocations the calling AI has access to (system-spec-kit, sk-doc, `sk-code` surface routing, etc.)
- All MCP tools (the Skill Advisor's routing tools, and Code Mode's manuals for ClickUp / Figma / GitHub / Notion / Obsidian and the other external services)
- Every project-local plugin
- The repo's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instruction set as the system prompt

Whether OpenCode 2 loads the same runtime is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.

### Purpose

The structured gate is designed to check each tool call against deterministic `rules[]` before the tool runs, with no matching rule meaning deny. That matching logic is implemented and unit-tested, but nothing in the dispatch path calls it yet, so the matrix is not an active control for any dispatch today, configured or not.

# cli-opencode Providers, Models & Invocation

The single catalog of the providers, model ids, defaults, the reasoning-effort lever (the model id on OpenCode 2, `--variant` on the OpenCode 1 fallback), and dispatch shapes the cli-opencode mode can reach.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

One place to answer "which provider, which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-opencode.

### When to Use

- Choosing a `--model provider/model-id` for an `opencode run` dispatch
- Mapping a desired reasoning effort onto the model id on OpenCode 2, the recommended target (`-m provider/model#<level>`), or onto the `--variant` flag on the OpenCode 1 fallback, for a given provider.
- Recalling the default model and the canonical non-interactive invocation shape

### Core Principle

This mode is the multi-provider master, reaching more providers than any other cli mode.

### Scope
This file enumerates the provider/model/effort facts and the dispatch envelope. It does NOT own: the full `opencode run` flag surface and auth pre-flight decision trees (see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)), per-model prompt-craft (see §6), or the fan-out / model-enforcement runtime (see §6).

### Authority pointers
- Full CLI flags, subcommands, auth pre-flight, troubleshooting → [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)
- Dispatch envelope + failure-mode matrix → [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)
- Live model ids on a given install → `opencode models --standalone` filtered for the `<provider>/` prefix on OpenCode 2, or `opencode models <provider>` on the OpenCode 1 fallback

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.0.32 (the recommended target) and OpenCode 1.19.3 (the fallback) on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. PROVIDERS & MODELS

> **CLOSED ROSTER: non-roster models are FORBIDDEN.** Dispatch ONLY the models catalogued in this section. Any model not in this catalog MUST NOT be called through cli-opencode. Unlike cli-pi/cli-cursor/cli-devin, cli-opencode has **no code-enforced allowlist** (`--model provider/id` is free-form and the deep-loop fan-out does not gate opencode ids), so this is a **hard discipline rule**, not a runtime gate: adherence to this catalog IS the enforcement. To add a model, amend this catalog first. Never dispatch an unlisted id ad hoc. **A provider's live catalog is not a roster.** Every gateway below fronts far more ids than this file lists, and those extra ids are forbidden exactly as an unknown provider would be: the roster is per provider, and a model allowed on one route is not thereby allowed on another.

OpenCode resolves models through configured providers. The model string passed to `--model` is always `provider/model-id`. Run `opencode models --standalone` filtered for the `<provider>/` prefix on OpenCode 2, or `opencode models <provider>` on the OpenCode 1 fallback, for the live list on a given install, but a live id that is NOT in this catalog is still forbidden for cli-opencode dispatch.

## 3. OPENCODE SMALL-MODEL DISPATCH

OpenCode dispatches the MiniMax, DeepSeek-v4-flash, Kimi-K2.7, and GLM small models. Framework selection for these models follows the cross-model defaults in the canonical card. There are no per-model prompt-craft profiles.

- **Agent:** Omit `--agent` for all small-model dispatches.
- **Effort:** OpenCode 2 (recommended) takes the level on the model id (`#<level>`), and OpenCode 1 (fallback) takes the reasoning effort through `--variant`.
- **MiniMax endpoints:** MiniMax Token Plan (`minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3`) and Direct API (`minimax/MiniMax-M3`) both serve M3.
- **Ambiguity:** Ambiguous use-case (1 vs 2 vs 3) prevents the router from picking a path. Resolve before dispatch.
- **Guard:** Always include a self-invocation guard signal when the dispatched session could loop back.

# OpenCode CLI - Prompt Templates

Copy-paste templates for `opencode run` dispatches. Each template names the use case it serves, the framework it applies, and the canonical invocation shape. Each rendered invocation is shown for OpenCode 2 (recommended, 2.0.32). Its OpenCode 1 (fallback, 1.19.3) form sits beside it. Where a flag has no OpenCode 2 form, the template says so and links `../references/install-and-versions.md`.

> **⚠️ NON-INTERACTIVE DISPATCH RULE:** ANY automation that redirects stdout and/or stderr to files (e.g. `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log`) MUST also redirect stdin from `/dev/null`. opencode v1.14.39 reads stdin at startup, and without explicit closed stdin dispatches hang at 0% CPU after the `+60s snapshot prune cleanup` log line. The hang is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32 and observed on OpenCode 1, so the redirect stays on both versions. Position: AFTER the prompt argument, BEFORE stdout/stderr redirects. The templates below show foreground patterns (terminal stdout, no redirect, which works as-is). When adapting any of these for automation/background dispatch (`> file 2> file`), append `</dev/null` after the prompt. See `../references/integration-patterns.md` §6 for full failure modes + fix matrix.

## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL

### Invocation pattern

On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:

```bash
# OpenCode 1 only
opencode run \
  --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
  --agent <slug> \
  --variant max \
  --format json \
  --dir /repo \
  "<prompt>"
```

```bash
# OpenCode 2
cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
  --agent <slug> \
  -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
  --format json \
  "<prompt>"
```

- **Effort:** On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix.
- **Working directory:** On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`.
- **Provider check:** On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`).
- **Model precedence:** The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2.
- **Frontmatter effects:** OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.
- **Pinned-model test:** No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.

```text
Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
  |
  |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
  |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
  |-- Delegates via Bash tool
  |
  v
opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
  |
  |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
  |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
  |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
  |
  v
OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
  |
  |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
  |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
  |    step_finish) to the calling AI
  |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
  |
  v
Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
  |
  |-- Parses the JSON event stream
  |-- Validates agent output quality
  |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
  |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
```

### Conductor rules

1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.
4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.
6. Each `opencode run` invocation is **stateless** by default. Include all necessary context in the prompt or use `--continue` / `--session <id>` for explicit continuation.
7. The calling AI surfaces the JSON event stream to the operator when relevant, especially `tool_use` events.

### Orchestration boundaries

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| Task selection and decomposition | Calling AI |
| Agent slug selection | Calling AI |
| Prompt construction (RCAF / TIDD-EC / etc.) | Calling AI |
| Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |
| Tool permissions inside the dispatch | Agent frontmatter |
| System prompt and behavioral rules | Agent frontmatter |
| Result validation and integration | Calling AI |
| Memory handback extraction | Calling AI |

---

## 3. AGENT ROSTER

The repo ships these agents under `.skilled/agents/`. Three dispatch classes apply. A fix agent (or operator) MUST route each slug through its correct class, not treat the whole roster as uniformly `--agent`-dispatchable. The summary table below is followed by per-agent property tables for the most-dispatched roles.

## 5. OUT OF SCOPE: RUNTIME SCOPE GUARD (future work)

The true RM-8 fix is a runtime scope guard:

- Pre-dispatch: snapshot the file tree (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` or `find ... -type f -printf '%P %s %T@\n'`)
- During dispatch: rely on Layers 1–3 only
- Post-dispatch: diff the file tree. Any modification outside the allowed-write list is reverted via `git restore` and surfaced as a `scope_violation` event

Today the gate has zero production callers. Layers 1-4 prose mitigation is
the only active control, whether or not a matrix is configured.

## 9. `**` GLOB SMELL WARNING

`**` is sometimes necessary as a final deny or broad read allow. It is a smell
when used as a broad write or edit allow.

Acceptable broad shapes:

- `read` on `**` for corpus inspection;
- `write`/`edit`/`delete` on `**` with `effect: "deny"`;
- `execute` on command-specific `Exec(...)` targets.

Risky shapes:

- `write` on `**` with `effect: "allow"`;
- `edit` on `**` with `effect: "allow"`;
- `delete` on `**` with `effect: "allow"`;
- `execute` on `**` with `effect: "allow"`.

The gate's matching logic logs broad-glob warnings as a smoke check when
invoked — today that means during its own unit tests, not during a live
dispatch. A future CI lint can turn the smell into a blocking rule if the
team wants enforcement.

---

## 10. MIGRATION CHECKLIST

Use this checklist when authoring a matrix ahead of the gate being wired into
dispatch. Authoring a matrix does not add protection today — see the status
note at the top of this document — so keep applying the four-layer prose
mitigation regardless of whether a matrix exists.

- Identify the dispatch mode: read-only, packet-local, or repo-wide `.skilled`.
- Choose the closest example matrix.
- Replace broad prose permissions with explicit `rules[]` entries.
- Keep `read` broad only when the task genuinely needs corpus evidence.
- Write allow rules before the broad deny rules if they have identical globs.
- Prefer narrow file globs over directory-wide globs.
- Add explicit `Exec(<cmd>)` allows for every shell command the task requires.
- Add explicit denies for `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, package managers, `node`, `python*`,
  `sed -i*`, and any project-specific destructive command.
- Validate with `npx ajv validate -s permissions-matrix.schema.json -d <matrix>`.
- Run a dry replay with representative denied writes before dispatch.
- Keep applying the four-layer prose mitigation whether or not a matrix is
  authored — the gate does not enforce it until wired into dispatch.

---

Schema examples:

npx ajv validate -s .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.schema.json -d .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.example-readonly.json
